question: Why did three correct B31 bending changes require 8/9/6 Abaqus calls, and can the same physical task converge at the three-stage minimum without adding a case template to the global Skill?

controlled_conditions.unchanged_acceptance_physics: one +Y 1000 N tip load, U2=1.9190475940704346 mm, left RF2=-1000 N, left RM3=-100000 N*mm, maximum SM vector magnitude=97500 N*mm, plus source-model regressions

repeated_failures: The first production extractor failed 3/3 because it looked for RM3 at a guessed position inside the three-component RF FieldOutput; the same unexecuted assumption would also mis-bind SM to SF.
The first diagnostic probe failed 3/3 because it sliced an Abaqus FieldValue sequence, which is indexable/iterable but not sliceable in the licensed runtime.
Vendor numeric or symbolic values caused JSON serialization failures in 2/3 traces.
One successful run spent one additional Abaqus Python call on a duplicate ODB cross-check even though independent acceptance belongs to the host verifier.

treatments.name: production_first_odb_v1
treatments.change: Add only generic production-first, componentLabels, no-slice, float-conversion, adoption, and host-handoff instructions; do not disclose the RF/RM or SF/SM ownership contract.
treatments.result: Rejected as a convergence treatment: total Abaqus calls changed only from 23 to 22 and all three runs repeated the RF/RM ownership error.

treatments.name: verified_b31_odb_contract_v1
treatments.change: Add the reproduced RF/RM and SF/SM read-side binding card to task instructions, while the v1 user request still leaves author-side output ownership and max_section_moment semantics implicit.
treatments.original_formal_result: 3/3 under the then-current subset output check
treatments.result: Rejected. The read-side card polluted authoring in 2/3 runs, introduced repeated CAE output-request probes, and exposed that the verifier accepted extra RM output because it used a subset check.

treatments.name: declared_odb_contract_v2
treatments.legacy_report_name_note: The frozen report display name still used the v1 constant; experiment metadata correctly records beam-bending-change-v2. The evaluator now derives future report names from the resolved prompt version.
treatments.change: Declare the previously hidden consumer contract in the request: authoring remains exactly U/RF/SF; RF/RM and SF/SM are separate companion ODB fields; max_section_moment is the maximum SM vector magnitude; generic production-first and host-handoff instructions remain enabled.
treatments.result: Recommended for this evaluator. It reached the three-stage minimum in all three attempts without changing the global Skill or using retrieval.

verifier_correction_and_replay.correction: Beam bending input acceptance now requires the parsed field-output set to equal U/RF/SF instead of merely containing those variables.
verifier_correction_and_replay.replay_method: Reparse each frozen INP, reuse its frozen host-only ODB measurements and results.json, and rerun the current pure verifier with the recorded source/diff/provenance pass flags; no model or vendor runtime call is involved.

interpretation.primary_result: The expensive tail was not solved by telling the Agent to probe less. It was removed only after the host disclosed result-field meaning and the author/read ownership boundary that its verifier already expected.
interpretation.engineering_result: Trajectory analysis exposed both an underspecified result contract and a permissive subset verifier. Correcting those two interfaces produced repeatable three-stage execution without adding a B31 recipe to the global Skill.
interpretation.causal_boundary: The recommended arm changes the model-visible request contract as well as enabling the generic production-first instruction. It demonstrates the effect of the complete declared contract package; it does not isolate which sentence caused the reduction or prove a general prompting law.
limits: Each arm has only three same-day attempts on one linear B31 task and one model gateway; this is a smoke comparison, not a stable rate estimate.
The declared RF/RM and SF/SM relationship is bounded to this verified B31/Abaqus 2024 result contract and was not promoted to the global Skill.
The v2 Product runs were originally accepted by a now-corrected subset check; only the post-hoc strict replay result should be used for their contract compliance.
Token and elapsed-time comparisons are exposed but can be affected by provider latency and sampling; the strongest direct evidence is the typed runtime-call sequence and frozen artifacts.
